bugs.title: [OVN] packet drops when provider network MTU exceeds tenant network MTU

blockers.summary: Regression mentioned: "…two commits in one to not introduce a regression by doing them separately. There were small changes required to unit tes…" (hudson-openstack)

The fix only takes effect when the non-default option ovn.ovn_emit_need_to_frag is enabled, so the SRU needs to say this and show it was tested with the option on. The comments contain no SRU template or verification for the Ubuntu series.

The upstream fix introduced a regression (bug #2105383, wrong network_ids filter in _gen_router_port_options), fixed by a follow-up commit. Any SRU must include both commits, as the stable/2024.x backports do, and not the original alone.

The stable/2024.1 and 2024.2 backports are squashed combinations with conflict resolutions and modified unit tests. They differ from the upstream master commits and need a careful review against the Ubuntu package version.

The effect also depends on the OVN version, since the N/S fragmentation behaviour is handled in OVN itself. The bug was reported on OVN 23.03, so it is unclear whether the Ubuntu OVN version supports gateway_mtu on the internal ports. No minimum OVN version is documented.

All earlier verification (CI run, 'verified' status) was done on the withdrawn .1 build. The re-spun package needs fresh verification in noble-proposed and a fresh verification tag. Reporters said they would retest once it is in noble-proposed.

A block-proposed-noble tag is still in place, and a bug-wide block-proposed tag was also blocking stonking migration. The qemu SRU depends on this fix and was also pulled from proposed, so ordering with qemu remains open.

The reviewer flagged that the patch Jorge authored carries 'Origin: backport' and must say 'Origin: upstream'. No updated debdiff or reply appears afterwards, so the resolute/stonking packaging may still need correcting.

The SRU test plan reproducer fails for the reviewer on resolute because tpm2-abrmd never becomes ready, and on stonking because engine_pkcs11 is not found. The test plan also lacks the apt install line for its dependencies. The fix therefore cannot be verified as written.
The reviewer asked for a PPA build with the patches so the contents can be reviewed and tested. No PPA link has been provided.

It is unclear whether the stonking upload is needed. OpenSSL 4 has no engine support, so the second patch is a no-op there. The regression is not tied to a specific OpenSSL 3.0.14 change. Without that, it is unclear that noble and jammy (OpenSSL 3.0.x, engines supported) are unaffected and need no SRU.

A user reported that, with the patches applied, libtss2-esys could not create RSA keys in the same process after the engine loaded a TPM key. That would make later wpa_supplicant re-authentications fail. The user later called this an unverified LLM hypothesis and cannot retest, so repeated connections remain untested.

The patches in d/p/series are not in upstream order, although upstream commit 6bde508 depends on 5894be2. The upstream URL uses a short hash rather than the full commit hash. Both were raised as optional fixes.

comments.author: whershberger
comments.body:
There are two standing issues with these patches:

- get_global_pool_hard_max_size parses /proc/sys/vm/max_map_count incorrectly, resulting in the default value being used unconditionally
- The default value returned by get_global_pool_hard_max_size is UINT_MAX; a better/conservative choice would be the kernel's default max_map_count (65530)

We've submitted upstream patches to resolve both of these issues; neither have been merged to qemu's master yet.

https://lists.gnu.org/archive/html/qemu-devel/2026-10/msg04337.html
